gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-002 diagnoses a missing normalization factor in the representation of curve normal cycles and its kernel pairing. Gold I001 concerns area factors in triangle-based surface quadrature and discrete currents; the shared presence of a scaling error does not identify the same object or failed quadrature operation.

ISSUE-003 explicitly computes the specified half-circle vector integral as 2β rather than (π/2)β and traces the resulting normalization through the cylindrical atom and pairing coefficient, exactly matching I002.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: Both identify the false half-circle integral normalization: the arc-length integral is 2β_T, not (π/2)β_T, so the cylindrical atom and its pairwise coefficient are mis-scaled.

component_coverage.gold_component: The specified semicircle has vector integral 2β_T rather than (π/2)β_T.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction gives the same arc-length parametrization and corrected value 2, explicitly rejecting the π/2 calculation.

component_coverage.gold_component: The erroneous integral propagates to cylindrical atom magnitudes, vector embedding, and the atom-pairing coefficient, changing π²/4 to 4.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction explicitly propagates the corrected integral through the cylindrical Dirac form, edge terms, and metric coefficient, identifying 4 instead of π²/4.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-001 addresses the abstract well-definedness of rectifiable-set currents under arbitrary orientation-reversing tangent-basis changes. Gold I004 concerns a specific displayed cylindrical basis that is claimed positive but is actually negatively oriented, and the resulting sign in the cylindrical tangent 2-vector; the general orientation topic does not establish recognition of that concrete formula error.

ISSUE-003 identifies an incorrect angular integral and cylindrical normalization. Gold I005 concerns replacing spatial edge integrals by midpoint values under an assumption that removes only spherical dependence, and then asserting an exact equality without quadrature remainders. These are different integration operations and obligations.
